title: A polynomial regarded as a formal power series
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $T$ an indeterminate. A polynomial $P=\sum_rc_rT^r\in R[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] is regarded as the formal power series $\sum_{n\geq0}c_nT^n\in R[[T]]$ [def-weil-formal-power-series] with the same coefficients (all but finitely many zero). This map $R[T]\to R[[T]]$ is an injective ring homomorphism preserving coefficients, in particular the constant coefficient $P(0)$. For $Z\in R[[T]]$ and $A,B\in R[T]$, the identity $BZ=A$ is meant in $R[[T]]$ through this map; when $B(0)$ is a unit of $R$, $B$ is a unit of $R[[T]]$ and $BZ=A$ says $Z=AB^{-1}$, i.e. $Z$ is the Taylor expansion at $T=0$ of $A/B$.
